label: D2 after a1 -> S1 (common), when the previous trial was unrewarded (mostly via a rare transition), late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a1 and reached S1 by a common transition (in_action == 1, in_state == 1; never on a2, S2, rare transitions, D1 or GO). Within those steps it is gated by the previous outcome: 94% of activation mass has prev_reward == 0, and the strongest activations follow an unrewarded rare trial (prev_common == 0 holds 68% of mass; prev_common == -1 is the window-start trial, where the previous trial is outside the window). It is almost absent before episode trial ~40 and grows over trials 40-99. Magnitude: activations near max on the first a1->S1c after an unrewarded trial, then a decaying tail (~0.1-0.2 of max) on the following a1->S1c trials after a reward, which accounts for most of the low-quartile misses. The base predicate (D2 & a1 & S1 & prev_reward==0 & ep_trial>=40) gets dev F1 0.69 / mass recall 0.94; adding prev_common != 1 lifts dev F1 to 0.75 (precision 0.79, mass recall 0.84). All variables are observed at D2. Not fully explained: precision and recall are incomplete, and the dependence on episode time suggests a slowly drifting hidden-state component.
